newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Weizman, PA's Arafat work on meeting.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Weizman, PA's Arafat work on meeting.

text.p: Israeli President Ezer Weizman and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat have agreed to meet but a date has yet to be set, a PLO official and Israel Radio said on Saturday.

"Weizman asked for the meeting," the PLO official, who confirmed the Israel Radio report and spoke on condition he not be identified, said. "No date has been set for the meeting. We don't expect it to take place before the end of the week."
He could not elaborate on the purpose of the meeting.
Weizman's director-general, Aryeh Shumer, later told Israel Radio that it was the Palestinian Authority that had requested the meeting.
"There are contacts on this issue and we are in contact with the prime minister and the Palestinian Authority in light of the request of the Palestinian Authority," Shumer said.

The news came just ahead of U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross's visit to the region which the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) official said is to begin on Monday night. Ross is trying to revive peace moves between the sides.

The Israeli president, whose position is largely ceremonial, has tried in the past to smooth relations between Israel and the Palestinian Authority that have been rocky since Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu took office last June.
Shumer said things would be clarified during the week, asking rhetorically why the sides should look far afield to Washington, France and Europe for mediation.
"The peace process has to be furthered," Shumer added.
Peacemaking ground to halt between the sides after Netanyahu sent bulldozers to carve out a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on March 18.
